title: .hns container — wire-harness interchange format
description: A .hns file is a ZIP archive (OPC/.docx-style). Its entries are described here as a single combined JSON document for validation convenience: {mimetype, manifest, meta, enrichment}. That combined object exists nowhere on disk -- to validate a single entry, use the corresponding definition directly, e.g. '#/definitions/manifest' for manifest.json. The archive MAY also carry one binary entry per meta.drawings[] record (path 'drawings/source/<file>' for a drawing authored by the sending party, or 'drawings/customer/<file>' for one supplied by the receiving party), STORED uncompressed, with provenance described by that array. Those binary entries are outside this JSON document's shape but are checked against meta.drawings[]. The archive SHOULD also carry a plain-text README.txt describing the specific file it is embedded in, per the specification's self-describing requirement; its absence is a warning, not a failure. NOTE: this schema documents field SHAPE only. The graph-theory invariants (root count, segments forming a tree, no double-booked connector pin, a wire's length agreeing with its path) are not expressible in JSON Schema and are specified in prose in spec/SPECIFICATION.md.

mimetype.description: Literal content of the archive's first entry, named 'mimetype', written STORED (uncompressed) so a reader can identify the container by reading only the first local file header, without decompressing or parsing the central directory -- the OPC/EPUB convention.

manifest.description: Archive entry manifest.json -- the harness graph inside a provenance envelope. `graph` is carried verbatim so meta.graphSha256 is a stable integrity anchor over topology alone, independent of any later enrichment.

schemaVersion.description: Incremented only on a breaking change to the shape of `graph`. Additive fields never require an increment.

harnessGraph.description: The harness topology, and the sole definition of it: nothing outside this object may introduce a node, segment, or wire. Structural invariants beyond field shape are specified in prose in spec/SPECIFICATION.md.

format.description: Identifies the topology model carried in this object. Required.

pn.description: Part number this harness definition describes. Required.

curated.description: True when the graph was authored or corrected by hand rather than derived automatically. Note this indicates origin, not verification -- see `confirmed`.

source.description: Free-text description of where this definition came from.

units.description: Unit for all length values in this graph. Inch-only at present.

notes.description: Free-text notes carried verbatim from the source drawing or definition.

flags.description: Markers recording that something is preliminary, a judgment call, or unconfirmed. Producers should carry these through rather than removing them.

confirmed.description: An explicit record that this definition was checked against the drawing on file and found accurate. Absent by default. A definition is not confirmed merely because it is `curated`, which indicates only that it was hand-authored. Consumers should re-check `drawingRev` against the drawing actually on file before relying on an older confirmation, since a drawing revision change invalidates it.

by.description: Who performed the check -- a name or initials.

drawingRev.description: Revision of the drawing this confirmation is pinned to.

hidePicture.description: Requests that consumers suppress automatically laid-out graphical views (schematic, pin-to-pin chart) for this harness, while still showing tabular data and any embedded drawings. Independent of `confirmed`: a definition may be entirely accurate and still produce a poor automatic drawing, because correctness and layout quality are separate concerns. This flag does not imply the data is wrong and is not a substitute for `confirmed`.

harnessGraphNode.description: A point in the harness: a connector, a branch point, a splice, or a termination.

root.description: Marks the node a consumer should treat as the origin when laying the harness out.

vendor_pn.description: The prevailing (vendor or customer) part number for the item at this node. This is the identifier intended for exchange between parties.

terminal.description: Free-text description of the termination at this node. Producers vary in what they place here; consumers should not attempt to parse it into structured fields.

pins.description: Number of positions, required when `type` is 'connector'. Positions are identified by number.

spliceKind.description: Set on a 'splice' node only when it is specifically a double-crimp ferrule joining two or more conductor legs to feed a single connector position. Distinct from a splice that extends a run or branches one run into two, which does not carry this field.

atConnector.description: For a splice or ferrule that physically inserts into a connector position, the connector node and position it lands in. This lets a consumer resolve the conductor's near end back to the real connector position, and merge conductors sharing that position into a single cell, rather than displaying the intermediate node. Optional; when absent, consumers display the node itself.

node.description: Id of the connector node this splice inserts into.

harnessGraphSegment.description: A span of the harness between two nodes.

length_in.description: Length of this span, in inches.

dim.description: Marks a span whose length is dimensioned on the drawing as a split measurement rather than a single value.

gauge.description: Conductor size. Values are AWG by convention; no unit is carried.

color.description: Insulation colour as free text. Producers vary between long and abbreviated forms, and the ordering of base and stripe is not defined by this schema -- consumers should not rely on either.

wireId.description: Printed identification marker on the physical conductor, when applicable.

length_in.description: Conductor length in inches. IMPORTANT: this schema does not state whether the value is a cut length or a length measured with terminals fully seated. Producers and consumers must agree on which is meant; see spec/SPECIFICATION.md.

path.description: Node ids the conductor traverses, in order. A single entry indicates both ends land on the same connector with no intervening span. Note this is a walk over nodes rather than a list of spans, so it does not always describe the conductor's true physical route.

node.description: Must equal the corresponding end of `path` -- the first entry for end1, the last for end2.

pin.description: Required when `node` refers to a connector. Positions are numbered from 1 and must not exceed that connector's `pins`. A position must not be occupied by more than one conductor, except where a ferrule node resolves several conductors to one position.

terminal.description: Free-text description of the termination at this end.

meta.description: Archive entry meta.json -- provenance and the integrity anchor.

rev.description: Revision of the harness definition, matching graph.rev.

generatedAt.description: Supplied by the caller rather than read from a clock during generation, so that regenerating the same input produces byte-identical output.

source.description: Identifier of the source definition this export was built from.

graphSha256.description: SHA-256 of manifest.graph, canonically serialized as JSON with sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace, UTF-8. IMPLEMENTERS PLEASE NOTE: that rule does not constrain how numbers are formatted, so a producer writing 18.0 and one writing 18 for the same value will compute different digests. Implementations in languages with a single numeric type may therefore disagree with one written in a language that distinguishes integers from floats. Pin your number formatting explicitly, and see spec/SPECIFICATION.md.

controlled.description: Whether this file is a controlled document. Always false: an export is uncontrolled once it leaves the producing system, and no controlled-export mode is defined.

origin.description: Structured form of the graph's free-text `source`, best-effort.

drawings.description: Provenance record for each drawing embedded as its own archive entry. Absent or empty when no drawing accompanies the definition.

unreleased.description: True when the drawing is preliminary or not yet released. Consumers must surface this rather than hide it.

arcname.description: Archive entry path holding this drawing's raw bytes, STORED uncompressed. The origin folder is vendor-neutral: 'source' for a drawing authored by the sending party, 'customer' for one supplied by the receiving party.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the embedded file's raw bytes, recomputable against the archive entry at `arcname`.

enrichment.description: Archive entry enrichment.json -- OPTIONAL. Additional identity and reference detail about entities already present in the graph. It never introduces or alters a node, segment, or wire, and is kept in a separate entry so that meta.graphSha256 does not have to account for changes to it.

ext.description: Graph-level detail extracted from the graph's own notes, for example an insulation temperature rating parsed from a note. Extracted only when unambiguous; the source note always remains present verbatim in the graph.

references.description: Part numbers cited in a node's free text that are not otherwise modelled as their own node or component. A pointer, not a resolved bill of materials.

enrichmentComponent.description: Additional detail about one node. Producers may carry private, organization-specific identifiers as additional properties; consumers must ignore properties they do not recognize, and must not expect them to be present.

approvedAlternates.description: Alternate parts already approved for this position, in structured form. Replaces free-text equivalence notes with a decided answer a consumer can act on.

terminalPartNumber.description: Part number extracted from the node's free-text `terminal` field.

terminalSpecRef.description: A reference to an external terminal specification, not a copy of it. Strip length and crimp height remain authoritative in the referenced document.

specRef.description: Identifier of the external specification document.

splicePartNumber.description: For a splice node, the splice or ferrule part number extracted from its label.
